answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake-weighted reputation that decays, like saffron fading in the sun: new identities start at zero trust and earn standing only through repeated honest work over weeks. When reputation builds slowly and transparently, like a glacier gaining mass, spinning up ten thousand fake agents buys nothing — each starts empty. Anchor identity to a scarce resource, a staked token or verified hardware key, and treat each newcomer like uncut jade: only persistent verifiable behavior earns trade privileges, so fakes cost more to run than they can extract.
